speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me, when did you first notice the rash on your newborn, and does the baby seem uncomfortable or feverish? 

Also, please describe the appearance of the rash in detail—is it flat or raised, and are the spots red, purple, or blanching when pressed? 

REQUEST TEST: CBC (Complete Blood Count) and CRP (C-Reactive Protein).

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details; the sparing of palms and soles is a key clue. Since I've already requested the CBC and CRP, do you have any results for those yet, or has the baby been exposed to any medications recently?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Toxicum Neonatorum
